summary: A 1977 specification of a remote job entry protocol for a resource sharing network, prepared for the Defense Communications Agency. Remote job entry means submitting batch work to a remote computer and getting results back.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 725 proposes a remote job entry protocol with three ways to send work and retrieve results. It is a preliminary document intended to gather comments, not a complete implementation specification.

questions: how do you submit jobs to remote computers
what are the three rje models in rfc 725
how would rje submit and retrieve jobs
subtitle: A preliminary proposal for submitting and retrieving remote batch jobs at different levels of service.

tldr.problem: The existing NETRJE protocol requires substantial software and creates a password-storage concern for unattended output delivery.
tldr.mechanism: The memo proposes three models: Telnet for commands and data, Telnet with a separate data connection, and FTP for transferring job files.
tldr.outcome: It provides a preliminary narrative and command definition to solicit comments; the authors say the protocol is not complete in every detail.

today: RFC 725 describes itself as an incomplete preliminary definition written to elicit comments and measure interest in adoption. It does not present the proposal as a finalized protocol.

sections.title: Why Propose Another RJE Protocol
sections.content:
The authors say the existing NETRJE protocol requires a user to implement User Telnet, Server FTP, and User RJE, and requires a server to implement the corresponding server and user roles. They identify the implementation burden and security concerns as reasons for proposing a different approach.

In particular, the existing approach to unattended output delivery requires storing a user's code and password at the remote server host. The proposal places that facility on the user system instead.
sections.plainLanguage: The authors want remote job entry to require less network software at user sites. They also want to avoid storing a user's remote password at the server for automatic output.

sections.title: Three Ways to Transfer Jobs
sections.content:
The Telnet-only model carries commands, replies, and data on one Telnet connection. The second model keeps control on Telnet but transfers job data over separate connections.

The FTP model transfers input and output files with FTP. The memo says sites can implement levels according to available resources and users can combine the models consistently.
sections.plainLanguage: One model uses Telnet for everything, one adds a separate data connection, and one uses FTP for files. The proposal allows implementations to support the level their resources permit.

sections.title: Commands and Job Measurements
sections.content:
The preliminary command list includes SCHED for submitting a job, OUTPUT for retrieving results, STATUS for checking session or job state, and commands such as CANCEL, ABORT, INDEF, and OUTDEF for control and transfer details. INPATH and OUTPATH provide server pathnames for FTP transfers.

MEASURE is proposed for returning job, session, or global measurements, including resource use and transfer information. The paper says its command and reply definitions are preliminary and not exhaustive.
sections.plainLanguage: The commands cover job submission, status, output, cancellation, and transfer settings. A proposed measurement command reports job, session, or overall information.
